title: A2-08 · The pluralities between: the most frequent patterns

blocks.text: A2-08 · The pluralities between: the most frequent patterns
Lesson overview

More than half of the Arab names form the plural not with a suffix ( ⁧ـُونَ⁩ , ⁧ـَات⁩ ) but changing the scheme of the word: ⁧كِتَاب⁩ → ⁧كُتُب⁩ , ⁧مَكْتَب⁩ → ⁧مَكَاتِب⁩ , ⁧وَزِير⁩ → ⁧وُزَرَاء⁩ . It is the plural over ( ⁧جَمْعُ التَّكْسِير⁩ , is broken plural). In A1 you have learned the plurals one by one; Here you learn to recognize the twelve most frequent patterns, which cover the vast majority of the plurals that you will encounter in the texts. Two practical rules guide everything: the plural is learned with the singular, and the scheme helps you to find the singular when you look for a word in the dictionary. Two weeks.

rows: A2 · Module A2.2 The name and the phrase
12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 62–63 of the calendar)

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Anki deck A2 (tag A2-08), voice synthesis script, tutor session in the second week
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. recognize the twelve most frequent plural patterns and bring a plural back to its singular;
2. actively use the plurals of the high-frequency words of the vocabulary A1–A2;
3. decline the diptotic plurals (fuʿalāʾ, afʿilāʾ, mafāʿil, mafāʿīl, fawāʿil, faʿāʾil);
4. to give adjectives and verbs with the plurals of people and things;
5. use collective names with their unit name ( ⁧تُفَّاح⁩ / ⁧تُفَّاحَة⁩ );
6. Shopping in the market and describing a place full of people and things.
Two-week plan.

2. Plural healthy or plural over?

There is no sure rule that says which plural takes a name: the dictionary always indicates the plural next to the singular (A2-01Section 7). But there are useful trends: the names of three consonants with short vowels ( ⁧كَلْب⁩ , ⁧وَلَد⁩ , ⁧قَلَم⁩ ) almost always have a plural over; long words with prefix ⁧مُـ⁩ which indicate people almost always take healthy plural ( ⁧مُدَرِّسُونَ⁩ ); prefix names ⁧مَـ⁩ of place take mafāʿil ( ⁧مَكْتَب⁩ → ⁧مَكَاتِب⁩ ).
3. The most frequent plural patterns

The first five families are 'triptote' and decline normally; the other seven are diptote (section 5). In the typical single column you will find the shape of the singular from which you usually start.

The rule is that of A1, but now it applies to many more plural:
things, animals, ideas, singular female institutions ⁧الشَّوَارِعُ⁩ · ⁧هٰذِهِ الوَثَائِقُ مُهِمَّةٌ.⁩ · ⁧المَكَاتِبُ الجَدِيدَةُ كَبِيرَةٌ.⁩

The plural of singular feminine things also applies to pronouns and demos: ⁧هٰذِهِ الكُتُبُ⁩ , ⁧الحَقَائِبُ⁩ … ⁧وَضَعْتُهَا⁩ I put the bags in. It is one of the most frequent mistakes of the italophonists: ⁧المَكَاتِبُ الجُدُدُ⁩ (adjective of people for things) or ⁧هٰؤُلَاءِ الكُتُبُ⁩ .
5. The plural diptotes
Six plural schemes are diptotic: they never take the tanwīn and, without article and without iḍāfa, have genitive in -a as the accusative (A1-19).

With the article or as the first term of aiḍāfa normally decline: ⁧فِي المَكَاتِبِ⁩ , ⁧فِي مَكَاتِبِ الوِزَارَةِ⁩ , ⁧مَعَ الأَصْدِقَاءِ⁩ . In texts without vowels, the diptototo is noted above all to the indeterminate accusative: no final alif ( ⁧كتبتُ رسائل⁩ , not * ⁧رسائلا⁩ ), while a triptoto has it ( ⁧كتبتُ كتبا⁩ ). A special case: the plurals in -in. The plurals as ⁧مَقَاهٍ⁩ Coffee (coffee) ⁧مَبَانٍ⁩ • buildings • ⁧أَرَاضٍ⁩ Land (A1) are defective: with the article ⁧المَقَاهِي⁩ , ⁧المَبَانِي⁩ , ⁧الأَرَاضِي⁩ . Recognize them as the names in -in of A1-15.

blocks.text: The collective is grammatically male singular: ⁧البُرْتُقَالُ لَذِيذٌ⁩ The oranges are good. It is used to talk about the thing in general or a quantity ( ⁧كِيلُو تُفَّاحٍ⁩ 1 kilo of apples; the unit name is used to count ( ⁧تُفَّاحَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ⁩ , ⁧ثَلَاثُ تُفَّاحَاتٍ⁩ ). The same mechanism you saw in A1 with ⁧نَبَات⁩ and in L0 with ⁧وَرْد⁩ .
7. From plural to singular (and dictionary)
In the texts you will meet many plurals of new words. The dictionary lists them under the root, next to the singular: you need to find the root. Proceed like this:
1. recognize the plural scheme (the added letters: ⁧أَ⁩ initial, ⁧ا⁩ or ⁧و⁩ or ⁧ي⁩ internal, ⁧ـَاء⁩ final, ⁧مَـ⁩ initial);
2. remove the letters of the scheme: three consonants remain;
3. look for the root and, under the root, the name that has that plural.
⁧سُجَنَاء⁩ fuʿalāʾ ⁧سَجِينس ج ن⁩ Incarcerated

The words of this table (except ⁧فُنْدُق⁩ ) are new: you don't have to learn them now, they serve to try the method. The names of four consonants ( ⁧فُنْدُق⁩ , ⁧دَفْتَر⁩ , ⁧مُهَنْدِس⁩ ...) do the plural with the scheme faʿālil ( ⁧فَنَادِق⁩ , ⁧دَفَاتِر⁩ ), also diptoto, or with the healthy plural ( ⁧مُهَنْدِسُونَ⁩ ).

8. Pronunciation

Long vowels from the pattern. The plurals are often distinguished from the singular only for a long vowel: kitāb / Kutub, rasūl / rusul; ʿāmil / ʿummāl. Listen to the B script and repeat in pairs. The final hamza of fuʿalāʾ and afʿilāʾ. wuzarāʾ, aṣdiqāʾ: ā long + glottis stroke. In front of a suffix the hamza remains: ⁧زُمَلَاؤُهُ⁩ zumalāʾuhu Your colleagues, ⁧أَصْدِقَائِي⁩ aṣdiqāʾī My friends. mafāʿil and mafāʿīl. makātib (short) / mafātīḥ (ī long): the length of the i distinguishes the two schemes.

⁧يَسْتَطِيعُونَ أَنْ يَدْفَعُوا الإِيجَارَ، وَتَرَكَ كَثِيرٌ مِنَ السُّكَّانِ القُدَمَاءِ مَنَازِلَهُمْ.⁩
